# AASH PLAYER

## Description
AASH PLAYER is a modern and feature-rich audio player application for Android devices. Designed with a focus on user experience and robust playback, it aims to provide seamless music enjoyment across various Android versions, supporting diverse audio formats and offering intuitive controls. The project involves developing a performant and stable media playback core, a sleek user interface, and handling common challenges like background playback, media library integration, and cross-device compatibility.

## Goals
- **Core Functionality:** Implement robust audio playback for common formats (MP3, WAV, FLAC, etc.).
- **User Interface:** Design and develop an intuitive and aesthetically pleasing UI/UX.
- **Playlist Management:** Allow users to create, edit, and manage playlists.
- **Background Playback:** Ensure smooth audio playback even when the app is in the background or the screen is off.
- **Compatibility:** Aim for broad compatibility across a range of Android versions, including older devices.
- **Performance:** Optimize for low resource consumption and fast response times.
- **Bug Resolution:** Identify and fix critical bugs, especially related to audio playback stability.

## Tech Stack
- **Language:** Kotlin
- **Platform:** Android (Android SDK, Android Jetpack Compose for UI)
- **Architecture:** MVVM or MVI
- **Media Playback:** Android MediaPlayer or ExoPlayer
- **Dependency Injection:** Hilt/Dagger
- **Local Storage:** Room Persistence Library
- **Version Control:** Git

### Progress Update (29-05-2026)
- Spent hours today trying to debug an audio glitch specifically affecting older Android versions within the AASH PLAYER code.
- The issue was thought to be resolved last week, but it is unfortunately still persisting, leading to significant frustration.
- Need to re-evaluate the previous fix attempts and potentially explore alternative solutions or deeper system-level debugging for older OS versions.

--- title: Obsidian Formatting Reference aliases: - Obsidian Cheatsheet - Markdown Guide - Obsidian Syntax tags: - obsidian - markdown - reference - formatting - cheatsheet created: 2026-06-04 updated: 2026-06-04 author: kittyboy06 type: reference status: complete --- # Obsidian Formatting Reference > [!abstract] About This Note > A complete, self-contained reference for everything you can write in Obsidian — from basic markdown to Obsidian-exclusive syntax, callouts, embeds, mobile shortcuts, and keyboard hotkeys. > Use the [[#Table of Contents]] to jump to any section. --- ## Table of Contents - [[#1. How Obsidian's Editor Works]] - [[#2. Headings]] - [[#3. Inline Text Formatting]] - [[#4. Lists]] - [[#5. Tasks & Checkboxes]] - [[#6. Links]] - [[#7. Embeds (Transclusion)]] - [[#8. Images]] - [[#9. Tables]] - [[#10. Code]] - [[#11. Blockquotes]] - [[#12. Callouts]] - [[#13. Math (LaTeX)]] - [[#14. Diagrams (Mermaid)]] - [[#15. Tags]] - [[#16. Frontmatter (Properties)]] - [[#17. Footnotes]] - [[#18. Miscellaneous Formatting]] - [[#19. Desktop Keyboard Shortcuts]] - [[#20. Mobile Shortcuts & Gestures]] - [[#21. Recommended Plugins]] --- ## 1. How Obsidian's Editor Works Obsidian has **three editor modes** — you can toggle between them via `Ctrl+E` or the mode switcher in the top-right corner of a note. | Mode | What It Does | | --- | --- | | **Source mode** | Raw markdown — you see the actual syntax characters | | **Live Preview** | Renders markdown as you type; cursor reveals raw syntax | | **Reading view** | Fully rendered, no editing possible | > [!tip] Recommended Setup > Use **Live Preview** (Settings → Editor → Default editing mode) for the best balance — you see rendered output while still writing markdown naturally. Obsidian stores every note as a plain `.md` file in your **vault** (a local folder on your device). This means your notes are never locked in — any text editor can open them. ### Key Concepts - **Vault** → The root folder containing all your notes and assets - **Pane / Tab** → A single note window; you can split panes side-by-side - **Graph View** → A visual map of all notes and their `[[wikilink]]` connections - **Backlinks** → Automatic reverse links — every note shows what links to it - **Block** → Any paragraph, heading, list item, or code block; can be linked via `^block-id` --- ## 2. Headings Use `#` symbols followed by a space. Obsidian supports H1 through H6. ```markdown # H1 — Page Title (use once per note) ## H2 — Major Section ### H3 — Subsection #### H4 — Minor Section ##### H5 ###### H6 ``` > [!note] Best Practice > Use `#` only **once per note** (matching the filename) — or skip H1 entirely and let the filename serve as the title. The **Outline** core plugin (View → Outline) auto-generates a table of contents from your headings. > [!tip] Folding Headings > Click the **arrow in the gutter** (left margin) to collapse/expand a heading section. Useful for long notes. Use `Ctrl+Shift+-` to fold all, `Ctrl+Shift+=` to unfold all. --- ## 3. Inline Text Formatting ### Bold ```markdown **bold text** __also bold__ ``` Renders as: **bold text** ### Italic ```markdown *italic text* _also italic_ ``` Renders as: *italic text* ### Bold + Italic ```markdown ***bold and italic*** ___also bold and italic___ ``` Renders as: ***bold and italic*** ### Strikethrough ```markdown ~~crossed out text~~ ``` Renders as: ~~crossed out text~~ ### Highlight (Obsidian-exclusive) ```markdown ==highlighted text== ``` Renders as: ==highlighted text== > [!warning] Highlight is Obsidian-only > The `==highlight==` syntax is not standard markdown — it won't render in GitHub, VS Code, or most other editors. ### Inline Code ```markdown Use `backticks` for inline code ``` Renders as: Use `backticks` for inline code ### Superscript & Subscript ```markdown x^2^ ← superscript (requires plugin or Pandoc) H~2~O ← subscript (requires plugin or Pandoc) ``` > [!info] Plugin Required > Superscript and subscript may require the **Markdown Formatting Assistant** plugin or a theme that supports it. Native support varies. ### Escape Characters To display a markdown character literally, prefix it with `\`: ```markdown \*not italic\* \# not a heading \[[not a wikilink\]] ``` --- ## 4. Lists ### Unordered (Bullet) Lists ```markdown - First item - Second item - Nested item (indent with 2 spaces or Tab) - Another nested item - Deeper nesting - Back to top level ``` You can also use `*` or `+` instead of `-` — all produce the same result. ### Ordered (Numbered) Lists ```markdown 1. First item 2. Second item 1. Nested numbered item 2. Another nested item 3. Third item ``` > [!tip] Auto-numbering > Obsidian auto-continues lists when you press Enter inside one. Press Tab to nest, Shift+Tab to unnest. The actual numbers in the source don't matter — Obsidian re-numbers them on render. ### Mixed Lists ```markdown 1. Step one - Sub-bullet under step one - Another sub-bullet 2. Step two ``` --- ## 5. Tasks & Checkboxes ### Basic Checkboxes ```markdown - [ ] Unchecked task - [x] Completed task ✓ ``` ### Extended Checkbox States (Obsidian-exclusive) ```markdown - [ ] Unchecked - [x] Completed - [/] In progress - [-] Cancelled - [>] Forwarded / Rescheduled - [<] Scheduled - [?] Question - [!] Important - [*] Star / Favourite - ["] Quote - [l] Location - [b] Bookmark - [i] Information - [S] Savings - [I] Idea - [p] Pros - [c] Cons - [f] Fire / Urgent - [k] Key - [w] Win - [u] Up arrow - [d] Down arrow ``` > [!info] Theme Dependent > Extended checkbox states are styled by your active **theme**. In source mode they all look the same — the visual differentiation appears only in Live Preview / Reading view. The **Tasks** community plugin can filter notes by checkbox state. > [!tip] Toggle in Reading View > In Reading view, you can **tap or click a checkbox** to toggle it complete/incomplete without switching to edit mode. --- ## 6. Links ### Internal Wikilinks (Obsidian-native) Wikilinks are the backbone of Obsidian's knowledge graph. They power backlinks, the Graph View, and the Outline panel. ```markdown [[Note Title]] ← Link to a note [[Note Title|Display Text]] ← Link with custom display text (alias) [[Note Title#Heading]] ← Link to a specific heading inside a note [[Note Title#^block-id]] ← Link to a specific block inside a note [[Note Title|Alias#Heading]] ← Alias + heading combo ``` **Creating a block ID:** ```markdown This is a paragraph I want to link to. ^my-block-id ``` Then link to it from another note: `[[This Note#^my-block-id]]` > [!tip] Wikilinks vs Markdown Links > Use wikilinks (`[[…]]`) for internal notes — they integrate with backlinks and the graph. Use standard markdown links (`[text](url)`) only for external URLs or maximum portability. ### External Links ```markdown [Link text](https://example.com) [Link with tooltip](https://example.com "Hover tooltip text") https://example.com ← Auto-linked bare URL ``` **Hotkey:** `Ctrl+K` to insert a link, `Ctrl+Shift+L` to insert an external link. ### Linking Between Vaults ```markdown [Open in another vault](obsidian://open?vault=MyVault&file=Note%20Name) ``` --- ## 7. Embeds (Transclusion) Embeds let you pull content from another note **live** into the current one. Any change to the source note updates everywhere it's embedded. ```markdown ![[Note Title]] ← Embed entire note ![[Note Title#Heading]] ← Embed just one heading's section ![[Note Title#^block-id]] ← Embed a single block ![[Note Title|Display Text]] ← Embed with alias (for display only) ``` > [!example] Use Case > Create a `Daily Log` note and embed `![[Project Status#Current Sprint]]` — every day's log automatically shows the latest sprint status without copy-pasting. --- ## 8. Images ### Local Images (in vault) ```markdown ![[image.png]] ![[image.png|400]] ← Set width to 400px ![[image.png|200x100]] ← Set width × height ![[image.png|alt text]] ← Alt text (accessibility) ``` ### External Images ```markdown ![Alt text](https://example.com/image.png) ![Alt text|300](https://example.com/image.png) ← Width override ``` > [!tip] Image Storage > Keep images in a dedicated subfolder like `Assets/` or `Attachments/` in your vault. Set this in Settings → Files & Links → Default location for new attachments. --- ## 9. Tables ### Basic Table ```markdown | Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | | -------- | -------- | -------- | | data | data | data | | data | data | data | ``` ### Alignment ```markdown | Left-aligned | Center-aligned | Right-aligned | | :----------- | :------------: | ------------: | | text | text | text | | text | text | text | ``` - `:--` → left align - `:--:` → center align - `--:` → right align > [!tip] Plugin Recommendation > Install the **Advanced Tables** community plugin for a much better table editing experience — it auto-formats columns, lets you Tab between cells, and adds a toolbar for table operations. --- ## 10. Code ### Inline Code ```markdown Use `console.log("hello")` inside a sentence. ``` ### Fenced Code Block ````markdown ```python def greet(name): print(f"Hello, {name}!") greet("Afsal") ``` ```` ### Supported Languages (examples) ```markdown ```python ```javascript ```typescript ```java ```kotlin ```swift ```c ```cpp ```rust ```bash ```shell ```zsh ```html ```css ```scss ```json ```yaml ```toml ```sql ```graphql ```markdown ```go ```ruby ```php ``` > [!info] Syntax Highlighting > Obsidian uses **PrismJS** for syntax highlighting. The available languages depend on your theme and whether you have syntax highlighting enabled (Settings → Editor → Syntax highlighting). --- ## 11. Blockquotes ### Basic Blockquote ```markdown > This is a quoted paragraph. ``` ### Nested Blockquotes ```markdown > First level quote. >> Second level — nested inside. >>> Third level. ``` ### Blockquote with Formatting ```markdown > **Important:** This is a bold statement inside a blockquote. > > It can span multiple paragraphs by adding a `>` before the blank line. ``` --- ## 12. Callouts Callouts are **Obsidian-exclusive** — they don't exist in standard markdown. They're built on blockquote syntax. ### Basic Syntax ```markdown > [!note] > Default callout with no custom title. > [!tip] Custom Title Here > Callout with a custom title. > [!warning] Watch Out > This is an important warning callout. ``` ### Collapsible Callouts ```markdown > [!note]+ Open by default (+ = expanded) > This content is visible by default but can be collapsed. > [!note]- Closed by default (- = collapsed) > Click the title to expand this callout. ``` ### All Built-in Callout Types | Type | Aliases | Colour | | ---- | ------- | ------ | | `[!note]` | — | Blue | | `[!abstract]` | `[!summary]`, `[!tldr]` | Teal | | `[!info]` | — | Blue | | `[!todo]` | — | Blue | | `[!tip]` | `[!hint]`, `[!important]` | Green | | `[!success]` | `[!check]`, `[!done]` | Green | | `[!question]` | `[!help]`, `[!faq]` | Yellow | | `[!warning]` | `[!caution]`, `[!attention]` | Orange | | `[!failure]` | `[!fail]`, `[!missing]` | Red | | `[!danger]` | `[!error]` | Red | | `[!bug]` | — | Red | | `[!example]` | — | Purple | | `[!quote]` | `[!cite]` | Grey | > [!example] Callout with Nested Content > You can put **any markdown** inside a callout — including lists, code blocks, and even other callouts. > > - Bullet point inside callout > - Another point > > ```python > print("code inside callout") > ``` --- ## 13. Math (LaTeX) Obsidian supports LaTeX math rendering via **MathJax**. ### Inline Math ```markdown The formula is $E = mc^2$ and it changed physics. The quadratic is $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$. ``` ### Block Math (Display Mode) ```markdown $$ \int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} $$ $$ \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} ax + by \\ cx + dy \end{pmatrix} $$ ``` ### Common LaTeX Symbols ```markdown \frac{a}{b} ← fraction \sqrt{x} ← square root \sum_{i=0}^{n} ← summation \int_{a}^{b} ← integral \alpha \beta \gamma \delta ← Greek letters \leq \geq \neq \approx ← comparison operators \rightarrow \leftarrow \Rightarrow ← arrows \infty \partial \nabla ← calculus symbols ``` --- ## 14. Diagrams (Mermaid) Obsidian has **native Mermaid support** — no plugin needed. ### Flowchart ````markdown ```mermaid graph TD A[Start] --> B{Decision?} B -- Yes --> C[Do This] B -- No --> D[Do That] C --> E[End] D --> E ``` ```` ### Sequence Diagram ````markdown ```mermaid sequenceDiagram Alice->>+John: Hello John! John-->>-Alice: Hi Alice! Alice->>John: How are you? John-->>Alice: Great, thanks! ``` ```` ### Gantt Chart ````markdown ```mermaid gantt title Project Timeline dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD section Phase 1 Task A :a1, 2026-06-01, 7d Task B :a2, after a1, 5d section Phase 2 Task C :2026-06-15, 10d ``` ```` ### Pie Chart ````markdown ```mermaid pie title Time Spent "Coding" : 45 "Debugging" : 30 "Documentation" : 15 "Meetings" : 10 ``` ```` ### Class Diagram ````markdown ```mermaid classDiagram class Animal { +String name +int age +speak() } class Dog { +fetch() } Animal <|-- Dog ``` ```` > [!tip] Live Preview > Mermaid diagrams render live in Live Preview mode. Use [Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live) to prototype before pasting into Obsidian. --- ## 15. Tags ### Inline Tags ```markdown This note is about #obsidian and #productivity and #pkm ``` ### Nested Tags (Hierarchical) ```markdown #project/musubi #project/arise-irl #project/portfolio #status/active #status/archived #type/reference #type/daily ``` > [!info] Tag Rules > - Tags cannot contain spaces — use `-` or `_` for multi-word tags > - Tags are case-insensitive (`#Obsidian` = `#obsidian`) > - Tags appear in the **Tags** panel in the left sidebar > - You can search by tag in the search bar: `tag:#obsidian` --- ## 16. Frontmatter (Properties / YAML) Frontmatter lives at the very top of a note, between `---` delimiters. It stores structured metadata. ### Full Example ```yaml --- title: My Note Title aliases: - Alt Name - Another Alias tags: - project - cs - active created: 2026-06-04 updated: 2026-06-04 author: kittyboy06 type: reference status: active priority: high related: - "[[Another Note]]" - "[[Yet Another Note]]" url: https://example.com rating: 4 publish: false --- ``` ### Common Property Types | Property | Type | Example | | -------- | ---- | ------- | | `title` | Text | `"My Note"` | | `aliases` | List | `[Alt, Shortname]` | | `tags` | List | `[obsidian, pkm]` | | `created` | Date | `2026-06-04` | | `status` | Text | `active / draft / archived` | | `type` | Text | `reference / daily / project` | | `rating` | Number | `1–5` | | `publish` | Boolean | `true / false` | > [!tip] Properties Panel > In Obsidian, frontmatter is displayed as a visual **Properties panel** at the top of the note (not raw YAML). Click any property to edit it. Toggle raw view via the three-dot menu. > [!note] Aliases > Aliases let you link to a note using a different name. `[[My Note]]` and `[[Alt Name]]` both resolve to the same note if `Alt Name` is listed in `aliases`. --- ## 17. Footnotes ### Inline Footnotes ```markdown This is a sentence with a footnote.[^1] [^1]: This is the footnote content. It can be placed anywhere in the document. ``` ### Named Footnotes ```markdown This is a sentence.[^my-note] [^my-note]: Named footnotes are easier to manage in long documents. ``` ### Inline Footnote (one-liner) ```markdown This is a sentence^[This footnote is defined inline — no separate reference needed.] ``` --- ## 18. Miscellaneous Formatting ### Horizontal Rule ```markdown --- *** ___ ``` All three produce a horizontal divider line. ### Line Breaks ```markdown First line (add two spaces at end for hard break) Second line on a new line Or leave a blank line between paragraphs for a paragraph break. ``` ### HTML in Obsidian Obsidian supports basic inline HTML (rendered in Reading view): ```html highlighted with HTML underlined text superscript subscript
centered text

(line break)   (non-breaking space) ``` ### Comments (Hidden in Reading View) ```markdown %% This is an Obsidian comment — invisible in Reading view and Publish %% %% Multi-line comments work like this %% ``` --- ## 19. Desktop Keyboard Shortcuts > [!info] Platform Note > All shortcuts below use `Ctrl` (Windows/Linux). On **macOS**, replace `Ctrl` with `⌘ (Cmd)`. ### Navigation | Action | Shortcut | | ------ | -------- | | Command palette | `Ctrl+P` | | Quick Switcher (open note) | `Ctrl+O` | | Search in vault | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | | Create new note | `Ctrl+N` | | Open settings | `Ctrl+,` | | Graph view | `Ctrl+G` | | Toggle left sidebar | `Ctrl+[` | | Toggle right sidebar | `Ctrl+]` | | Navigate back | `Ctrl+Alt+←` | | Navigate forward | `Ctrl+Alt+→` | | Open in new tab | `Ctrl+Enter` (from Quick Switcher) | | Close current tab | `Ctrl+W` | ### Editing | Action | Shortcut | | ------ | -------- | | Bold | `Ctrl+B` | | Italic | `Ctrl+I` | | Insert wikilink | `Ctrl+K` (then type note name) | | Insert external link | `Ctrl+Shift+L` | | Toggle checklist | `Ctrl+L` | | Indent list item | `Tab` | | Unindent list item | `Shift+Tab` | | Duplicate line | `Ctrl+D` | | Delete line | `Ctrl+Shift+K` | | Undo | `Ctrl+Z` | | Redo | `Ctrl+Y` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` | | Select all | `Ctrl+A` | | Find & replace | `Ctrl+H` | ### View & Workspace | Action | Shortcut | | ------ | -------- | | Toggle Reading / Edit mode | `Ctrl+E` | | Fold all headings | `Ctrl+Shift+-` | | Unfold all headings | `Ctrl+Shift+=` | | Toggle spell check | `Ctrl+Shift+S` | | Zoom in | `Ctrl+=` | | Zoom out | `Ctrl+-` | | Reset zoom | `Ctrl+0` | | Split pane vertically | `Ctrl+\` | | Split pane horizontally | `Ctrl+Shift+\` | > [!tip] Custom Hotkeys > Go to **Settings → Hotkeys** to remap any command to your preferred key combination. You can also search for commands by name in the hotkeys panel. --- ## 20. Mobile Shortcuts & Gestures ### Touch Gestures | Action | Gesture | | ------ | ------- | | Switch Reading ↔ Edit mode | Double-tap on the note | | Reveal navigation bar | Scroll up or tap near the top | | Auto-hide navigation | Scroll down | | Open left sidebar | Swipe right from the left edge | | Go back (in settings) | Swipe right | | Toggle a checkbox | Tap the checkbox in Reading view | | Select text | Long-press → drag selection handles | | Open context menu | Long-press on text | ### Format Toolbar (Above Keyboard) When you enter editing mode on mobile, Obsidian shows a **format toolbar** above the on-screen keyboard. **Default toolbar buttons:** Bold · Italic · Insert link · H1 · H2 · H3 · Bullet list · Numbered list · Checkbox · Indent · Unindent · Undo · Redo **Customise the toolbar:** Settings → Mobile → Toolbar — add, remove, or reorder any Obsidian command. > [!tip] Tablet Behaviour > On tablets (as of Obsidian Mobile v1.11, Dec 2025), the toolbar is **center-aligned** for better ergonomics on wider screens. ### Android App Shortcuts (Android 7.1+) Available since Obsidian Mobile v1.11: | Action | How To | | ------ | ------ | | Open a specific note | Long-press app icon → tap shortcut | | Open Daily Note | Long-press app icon → tap shortcut | | Add shortcut to home screen | Drag shortcut icon from long-press menu to home | | Find via launcher | Search bar on most Android launchers | > [!warning] Not Yet Configurable > As of v1.11, Android app shortcuts are fixed to "Open note" and "Daily note" — custom shortcut targets are not user-configurable yet. --- ## 21. Recommended Plugins ### Core Plugins (Built-in, toggle in Settings → Core Plugins) | Plugin | What It Does | | ------ | ------------ | | **Backlinks** | Shows all notes that link to the current note | | **Outgoing links** | Shows all links from the current note | | **Outline** | Auto-generates a TOC from headings | | **Templates** | Insert pre-written note templates | | **Daily notes** | Creates a new note for each day | | **Canvas** | Infinite spatial whiteboard for connecting notes | | **Bases** | Database-style view for notes (v1.9+) | | **Search** | Full-text vault search | | **File recovery** | Auto-saves snapshots of your notes | | **Quick switcher** | `Ctrl+O` note launcher | | **Graph view** | Visual link map of your entire vault | | **Tag pane** | Browse all tags in sidebar | ### Community Plugins (install via Settings → Community Plugins) | Plugin | Use Case | | ------ | -------- | | **Advanced Tables** | Tab-to-move, auto-format, toolbar for tables | | **Commander** | Customise mobile toolbar icons; add commands to ribbon | | **Editing Toolbar** | Rich formatting bar with 30+ formatting actions | | **Tasks** | Filter, sort, and schedule checkbox tasks across notes | | **Dataview** | Query your vault like a database (`TABLE`, `LIST`, `TASK`) | | **Templater** | Powerful template engine with JS scripting | | **Calendar** | Weekly/monthly view linked to daily notes | | **Obsidian Git** | Auto-backup vault to a GitHub repo | | **Kanban** | Kanban boards inside your vault | | **Excalidraw** | Full whiteboard / sketching inside Obsidian | | **Mind Map** | Render a note as an interactive mind map | | **Linter** | Auto-format and lint your markdown on save | | **Recent Files** | Quick-access list of recently opened notes | | **Local REST API** | Expose your vault over localhost API (great for BrainOS-style integrations) | > [!tip] Plugin Safety > Community plugins run JavaScript locally. Only install plugins with a large download count and active maintenance. Review the plugin's GitHub before installing. --- > [!quote] Philosophy > *"Obsidian is a tool for thought — the notes you make here are yours, stored as plain text, readable forever, portable to any editor. Format them so they serve your thinking, not the other way around."* --- *Last updated: 2026-06-04 · Vault: ObsidianCloud · Author: [[Afsal Ahmed]]*

title: LocalCrafts.md
content:
---
# LocalCrafts

## Description
LocalCrafts is an exciting new side project inspired by Sabu's vision for a dedicated local e-commerce platform. The goal is to create a vibrant online marketplace where local artisans and crafters can easily showcase and sell their unique, handmade goods directly to their community. This project aims to empower local talent, foster economic growth within the region, and provide consumers with a convenient way to discover and purchase handcrafted items, reducing the reliance on larger, more impersonal marketplaces.

## Goals
- **MVP (Minimum Viable Product):** Launch a basic functional platform allowing artisans to list products and customers to browse and purchase.
- **User Experience:** Design an intuitive and visually appealing interface for both sellers and buyers.
- **Local Focus:** Implement features that highlight the local origin of products and sellers.
- **Community Engagement:** Foster a sense of community among local crafters and customers.

## Tech Stack
-   **Frontend:** React / Next.js (for server-side rendering and SEO)
-   **Backend:** Node.js (Express) / Python (Django/Flask)
-   **Database:** PostgreSQL (for relational data)
-   **Cloud Platform:** Vercel (for frontend deployment) / AWS / DigitalOcean (for backend & database)
-   **Payment Gateway:** Stripe / PayPal integration
-   **CMS (Optional for product management):** Strapi / Sanity.io

### Progress Update (29-05-2026)
-   Initiated 'LocalCrafts' as a new side project, drawing inspiration from Sabu's idea for a local e-commerce platform focused on handmade goods.
-   Began the initial design phase by mentally sketching UI wireframes and user flows for the site.

## Project: My Life Updates

### Description
This vault entry serves as a dedicated space for chronicling the ongoing journey of life, capturing moments of growth, challenge, reflection, and discovery. It is a living document of personal evolution, providing a sanctuary for thoughts, emotions, and insights gleaned from the daily ebb and flow of existence. Here, Afsal can openly express their experiences, track their mental and emotional landscape, and reflect on their path forward.

### Goals
*   **Self-Reflection & Awareness:** To foster deeper understanding of personal motivations, struggles, and triumphs.
*   **Emotional Processing:** To provide an outlet for expressing and processing complex emotions, from joy to sadness, frustration to inspiration.
*   **Growth Tracking:** To document personal development, learning experiences, and shifts in perspective over time.
*   **Problem Identification:** To identify recurring patterns, challenges, or sources of unease, paving the way for targeted self-improvement strategies.
*   **Purpose & Direction:** To regularly reflect on life's overarching purpose and current direction, aiding in decision-making and goal setting.

### Tech Stack
*   **Obsidian.md:** The primary platform for note-taking and knowledge management.
*   **Daily Notes Plugin:** For consistent daily reflections and linking to this project note.
*   **Dataview Plugin:** Potentially for querying and surfacing insights from logged entries over time.

### Progress Update (29-05-2026)
*   Experienced a significant struggle with procrastination and self-doubt, leading to a feeling of being stuck.
*   Noted a general lack of motivation for projects and an overarching sense of unease.
*   Identified a strong need for self-reflection regarding current life direction and purpose.
*   Expressed a desire to 'escape this feeling of being stuck,' indicating a need to actively document personal struggles and growth.
*   Currently experiencing significant exhaustion and feeling mentally drained, likened to a 'zombie.'
*   Had a vivid dream about the childhood home, which evoked strong feelings of nostalgia and sadness, pointing to deeper emotional processing.
